facts.statement: The holotype braincase of Bissektipelta was excavated in September 1998 by a joint Uzbek-Russian-British-American project.
facts.quote: In September 1998, the joint Uzbek-Russian-British-American-Project excavated the braincase of an ankylosaur.

facts.statement: Jolyon Parish and Paul Barrett renamed the genus from Amtosaurus to Bissektipelta in 2004 after determining the original genus was a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: In 2004, Jolyon Parish and Paul Barrett concluded that the type species of Amtosaurus, Amtosaurus magnus, was a nomen dubium, a dubious name.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected from the Bissekty Formation at Dzharakuduk, dating to the late Turonian-Coniacian.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, ZIN PH 1/6, was collected from the Bissekty Formation, dating from the late Turonian-Coniacian, of Dzharakuduk.

facts.statement: The top of the Bissektipelta skull roof features grooves forming a truncated "Y" shape that separate three polygonal areas of bone tissue.
facts.quote: On the top skull roof grooves are present, together forming a truncated "Y" and separating three polygonal areas of flat remodelled bone tissue.

facts.statement: A complex network of vascular canals around the skull roof allowed Bissektipelta to redistribute blood flow to cool its brain and maintain optimal temperatures.
facts.quote: The numerous small vascular canals around the skull roof, the lateral wall of the brain case and cranial vessels form a complex network around the brain which allowed the redistribution of the blood flow and physiological mechanisms for heat exchange in order to cool-down the brain and maintain optimal temperatures.

facts.statement: The length of the cochlear ducts suggests Bissektipelta was adapted for low-frequency hearing between 100 Hz and 3000 Hz.
facts.quote: The length of the cochlear ducts in the inner ear suggests that Bissektipelta, and many other ankylosaurs, were adapted for low frequency-hearing within 100 Hz and 3000 Hz.

facts.statement: Victoria M. Arbour and Philip J. Currie affirmed that Bissektipelta belongs within the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: However, Victoria M. Arbour and Philip J. Currie affirmed the position within the Ankylosauridae.

facts.statement: Bissektipelta lived during the Turonian stage, approximately 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Bissektipelta is a genus of ankylosaurine thyreophoran dinosaurs that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous.
rejected.quote: Bissektipelta (meaning "Bissekty shield") is a genus of ankylosaurine thyreophoran dinosaurs that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous in what is now the Bissekty Formation of Uzbekistan.

rejected.statement: Research in 2019 suggested Bissektipelta had a well-developed sense of smell, poor hearing and eyesight, good taste sensitivity, an omnivorous diet, and the unusual ability for filter-feeding.
rejected.quote: In 2019, Alifanov and Saveliev redescribed the braincase noting that Bissektipelta had a well-developed olfaction, poor hearing and eyesight, good taste sensitivity, omnivorous diet and the unusual ability for filter-feeding.
